previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for green sputum from her tracheostomy, chest and throat pain, chills, and odynophagia. She had recently completed a course of outpatient vancomycin for MRSA tracheitis. On admission, she was unable to swallow pills due to pain and required IV morphine. Evaluation showed no fever, leukocytosis, or radiographic abnormalities. Sputum culture revealed gram-positive cocci, and she was treated with intravenous vancomycin. Her symptoms improved, and she was transitioned to oral doxycycline. Blood cultures remained negative. She was discharged home on a 10-day course of doxycycline and ondansetron for nausea, with follow-up planned with infectious disease and pulmonary specialists for possible MRSA decolonization.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period
Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere

INDICATION:  ___ with trach history of tracheobronchitis now with cough and
dysphagia  // assess lungs, trachea,  and esophagus

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: 

Left chest wall port is again seen.  The lungs are clear without
consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax.  Tracheostomy tube is in stable
position.  No acute osseous abnormalities.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute cardiopulmonary process.  No focal consolidation.

EXAMINATION:  CT NECK W/CONTRAST (EG:PAROTIDS) Q22 CT NECK

INDICATION:  Evaluate for possible post pharyngeal or esophageal lesions at
may contribute to odynophagia, in a ___ woman with a chronic
tracheostomy secondary to tracheobronchomalacia, chronically colonized with
MRSA, status post multiple admissions for tracheitis, now presenting with
odynophagia, increased sputum, and dyspnea on exertion.

TECHNIQUE:  Imaging was performed after administration of 70 ml of Omnipaque
intravenous contrast material.

MDCT acquired helical axial images were obtained from the thoracic inlet
through the skull base.

Coronal and sagittal multiplanar reformats were then produced and reviewed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 7.2 s, 27.5 cm; CTDIvol = 14.6 mGy (Body) DLP = 379.8
mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 2.0 s, 7.9 cm; CTDIvol = 11.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 74.8
mGy-cm.
   3) Spiral Acquisition 1.6 s, 6.7 cm; CTDIvol = 13.5 mGy (Body) DLP = 69.3
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 545 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Contrast-enhanced CT neck from ___.

FINDINGS: 

Again noted is a tracheostomy, with the tube terminating in the upper thoracic
trachea, unchanged in position.  There is again deformity of the laryngeal and
tracheal cartilage, with stenosis just superior to the level of the
tracheostomy, similar in appearance compared to ___.  Asymmetric
increased prominence of the right false vocal cord is also similar in
appearance compared to ___.  Oropharyngeal airway remains collapsed,
likely secondary to the tracheostomy.  There is no evidence for a mass,
inflammatory change, or organized fluid collection in the neck.

The salivary glands enhance normally and are without mass or adjacent fat
stranding.  A left parotid 12 mm oval nodule, probably a lymph node, on image
3:29 is stable dating back to the earliest available comparison exam from ___.  The thyroid gland again demonstrates a subcentimeter
hypodensity in the upper pole of the left lobe. Cervical lymph nodes are
prominent, but not pathologically enlarged by CT size criteria. The neck
vessels are patent.

Visualized upper lungs appear clear.  No concerning bone lesion is seen.

There is mucosal thickening opacifying a single right anterior ethmoid air
cell.  Other paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are well aerated.  This
exam is not technically optimized for evaluation of the included brain
parenchyma, but no concerning abnormality is seen on limited evaluation.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence for new inflammatory change or fluid collection to explain the
patient's symptoms.
2. Unchanged appearance of the tracheostomy.  Unchanged deformity of the
laryngeal and tracheal cartilage resulting in stenosis of the airway just
superior to the level of the tracheostomy.
3. Unchanged prominence of the right false vocal cord compared ___.
